explain.say: Imagine you had to explain how to tie a shoelace every single time you wanted someone to do it. Tiring! It is easier to teach it once, give it a name, and then just say tie your laces. That is a function. Look at the first box: we define draw square once.

explain.say: Now look at the second box. To use it, you call it by name: draw square, 50. Calling means asking the function to run. The steps inside run, and a square appears. How many times could you call it?

explain.say: Look at the board: without functions you copy the same lines again and again, and one mistake means fixing it everywhere. With a function you write it once and call it many times. Which way would you rather fix?

left.title: Copy and paste
points: A bug must be fixed 3 times

explain.say: Brilliant! Functions can also give an answer back, called a return value, like a calculator that returns the total. Wow fact: apps are built from thousands of small functions, each doing one job. Challenge: invent a function called make tea. What parameter would it need?

faq.q: What is a function in programming?
faq.a: A function is a named block of code that does one job. You write it once and then run it whenever you need it by calling its name.
asks: What is a procedure in coding?

faq.q: What does calling a function mean?
faq.a: Calling a function means telling the program to run it, by writing its name and any inputs in brackets, like draw_square(50).
asks: How do you use a function?

faq.a: A parameter is a named input inside a function. When you call draw_square(50), the parameter size takes the value 50, so the same function can draw squares of any size.
asks: What is an argument in coding?
What goes in the brackets of a function?

faq.a: Functions save repeating code, make programs shorter and easier to read, and mean a bug only needs fixing in one place. They also let teams share jobs.
asks: What are the benefits of functions?
Why not copy and paste code?

faq.a: A return value is the answer a function sends back. A function add(2, 3) might return 5, which the program can then store or print.
asks: Can a function give back an answer?

facts: Programming languages call reusable code blocks functions, procedures, subroutines or methods.
In Python a function is defined with the word def, for example def draw_square(size):.

quiz.say: You call draw square with 30. What is the parameter size inside the function?
quiz.why: The value in the brackets is passed into the parameter, so size is 30.

wrong.1: 4 is how many sides it draws, not the size.
wrong.2: 90 is the turning angle, not the input.

quiz.say: What is the biggest advantage of putting repeated code in a function?

options.show: You write and fix the code in one place
options.say: You write and fix the code in one place

quiz.why: Writing it once means less code and one place to fix bugs.

wrong.1: Functions do not change the computer.
wrong.2: You still need to test functions.
